body:
Global crypto markets held broadly constructive on 2026-08-04, though the session carried an unmistakable undercurrent of anxiety. Total market cap sits at $2.26T, up 0.91% over the past 24 hours, on aggregate volume of $55.5B. BTC dominance at 56.4% and ETH dominance collapsing to 9.9% tell you the narrative right now: capital is not rotating freely through the risk curve, it is bunching at the top while pockets of speculative interest spark in select mid-caps. The Fear and Greed Index printing 25, Extreme Fear, down from 28 yesterday, confirms that whatever gains we are seeing are being bought into with reluctance. This is not a market flush with conviction.

Bitcoin at $63,490 is the anchor of the session, printing a 24-hour gain of 1.60% on $25.13B in volume, which is respectable participation without being exceptional. The 7-day picture is essentially flat at +0.10%, meaning the weekly tape is one long consolidation wrapped in intraday noise. A CoinDesk headline has the figure closer to $63,600 in their live tracker, consistent with the range we are operating in. The level to watch on the upside is the psychological $65,000 handle, which has repeatedly capped rallies in recent sessions; a clean close above there on meaningful volume would shift near-term sentiment. On the downside, a failure to hold $62,000 would open up a retest of levels that would further erode confidence already sitting at Extreme Fear. Jim Cramer's quantum computing panic, referenced in headlines, has clearly not dented price, which is itself modestly bullish signal-to-noise filtering.

Ethereum at $1,853.74 continues to underperform its headline peer, gaining only 0.80% on the day against BTC's 1.60% and printing a 7-day loss of 1.40%. That divergence is meaningful and aligns with ETH dominance at 9.9%. The genuine standouts in the altcoin space are ADA, AVAX, and DOT. ADA is the session's loudest voice at +6.60% on the day and an extraordinary +24.10% on the 7-day, with $0.69B in volume suggesting real participation, not just thin-market drift. AVAX is up 5.80% in 24 hours and 5.20% on the week at $6.77, while DOT has quietly built a 10.00% 7-day return to trade at $0.836778. On the negative side, UNI is the worst performer tracked, down 4.50% on the day to $3.87 despite a positive 7-day of 4.70%, suggesting yesterday's strength is being unwound fast. LINK is also soft at -0.80% to $8.13, down 2.00% on the week. BNB at $588.42 is quietly one of the more stable performers at +4.20% on the week. SOL at $73.16 is essentially unchanged on the 7-day with a 24-hour gain of 1.20%, and a governance proposal to ramp SOL daily burns from $47,000 to $650,000 is circulating, which is a supply-side catalyst worth tracking.

Macro context is the most important variable in today's session and it is not clean. US intervention in yen markets to address carry-trade dynamics is the dominant headline risk, referenced by both CoinDesk and Cointelegraph, and the mechanism is straightforward: a sharp yen move forces leveraged carry unwinds across risk assets, draining the exact liquidity that has been supporting crypto in the $60,000-65,000 range. This is not hypothetical; the 2024 carry-trade shock remains fresh in institutional memory and any repeat would put BTC on notice. On the regulatory side, a New York judge denying the CFTC's motion to halt enforcement action against Kalshi is a nuanced data point, suggesting courts are willing to push back on aggressive agency overreach, which is marginally constructive for the broader crypto regulatory outlook. Nigeria formalizing crypto tax collection rules adds to the global trend of states treating digital assets as a legitimate revenue stream rather than an existential threat. Bhutan's GMC deploying its 10,000 BTC pledge into active treasury management also reinforces sovereign-level buy-and-hold behavior at the institutional margin.

Looking ahead, the yen situation is the single largest near-term risk and deserves the most attention. If carry-trade fears escalate into actual forced deleveraging, crypto will not be insulated regardless of on-chain fundamentals. Watch BTC's ability to hold above $62,000 as the first stress indicator. A recovery through $65,000 on volume above the 24-hour average of $25.13B would be the clearest signal that the consolidation is resolving higher. The ADA and DOT moves need confirmation; a second day of volume-supported gains would validate the rotation, while a single-session reversal would flag them as noise. The Telegram situation, with Apple briefly removing the app and Gram rebounding per Cointelegraph, is worth monitoring as a sentiment proxy for censorship-resistance narratives that have historically benefited crypto. The new RLUSD lending pool for XRP holders on Ethereum, cited at $280 million in the headline, is a DeFi liquidity development that could quietly support XRP volumes beyond today's modest +0.60%. Fear and Greed at 25 means the market is priced for bad news; any macro clearing event upgrades the asymmetry to the upside fast.
